trigger: applied Cauchy-Schwarz to (E[XY])^2 <= E[X^2] E[Y^2]
symptom: step asserts the bound without verifying both second moments are finite
root_cause: Cauchy-Schwarz requires E[X^2] < infinity and E[Y^2] < infinity; step ignored the finite second moment hypothesis
resolution: explicitly check E[X^2] < infinity and E[Y^2] < infinity before invoking the inequality; if not, fall back to a truncation argument

trigger: applied Jensen's inequality to a non-convex function
symptom: step claims phi(E[X]) <= E[phi(X)] but phi is concave or non-convex
root_cause: Jensen requires phi convex for the <= direction and concave for the >= direction
resolution: verify convexity (or concavity) of phi on the support of X and orient the inequality accordingly; for sigmoid-like maps split the domain

trigger: Jensen's inequality with reversed direction
symptom: the chain of inequalities went the wrong way and the conclusion is vacuous
root_cause: concave phi gives phi(E[X]) >= E[phi(X)], not <=
resolution: redo the argument with the correct concave Jensen, or flip phi to -phi to land in the convex case

trigger: Markov's inequality applied to a signed random variable
symptom: the bound is trivial or negative
root_cause: Markov requires non-negativity of the random variable being bounded
resolution: apply Markov to |X| or to a non-negative transform such as e^{lambda X}; reformulate as a Chernoff-style bound

trigger: applied Holder's inequality with non-conjugate exponents
symptom: the algebraic identity 1/p + 1/q = 1 is missing or wrong
root_cause: Holder requires conjugate exponents p, q with 1/p + 1/q = 1
resolution: set p and q so that 1/p + 1/q = 1; for triple products use generalised Holder with three exponents summing reciprocally to one

trigger: Minkowski applied for p < 1
symptom: triangle-like inequality used in L^p with p < 1 in the additive form
root_cause: Minkowski (subadditivity) holds for p >= 1; for p < 1 only the quasi-norm relation holds with extra factors
resolution: switch to the |x + y|^p <= |x|^p + |y|^p inequality for 0 < p < 1, or restrict the argument to p >= 1

trigger: swapped limit and integral without dominated convergence
symptom: lim integral f_n equates to integral lim f_n with no dominating function or monotonicity
root_cause: DCT/MCT was invoked without verifying the integrable dominating function or monotonicity
resolution: produce an integrable g with |f_n| <= g a.e., or check monotonicity for MCT; if neither, use Vitali plus uniform integrability

trigger: interchanged differentiation and integration without uniform domination
symptom: d/dx integral f(x, t) dt = integral d/dx f(x, t) dt invoked without bound on |partial f|
root_cause: Leibniz rule requires a uniformly integrable bound on the derivative
resolution: establish |partial_x f(x, t)| <= g(t) with integrable g on a neighbourhood of x; then DCT justifies the swap

trigger: applied Fubini to a non-integrable function
symptom: swapped order of double integral while integrand changes sign and is not integrable
root_cause: Fubini requires absolute integrability over the product measure; only Tonelli works for non-negative integrands
resolution: verify integral integral |f| dmu dnu < infinity; if only one integrand is non-negative, use Tonelli for that part

trigger: convergence in distribution treated as convergence in probability
symptom: step uses joint convergence X_n -> X and Y_n -> Y from convergence in distribution alone
root_cause: convergence in distribution does not give joint convergence of pairs; convergence in probability is needed for that
resolution: either use Slutsky when one limit is a constant, or upgrade to almost sure or in-probability convergence via Skorokhod representation

trigger: convergence in probability treated as almost sure
symptom: step claims P(X_n -> X) = 1 from convergence in probability
root_cause: convergence in probability does not in general imply almost sure convergence
resolution: extract an a.s. convergent subsequence via Borel-Cantelli or use uniform integrability if L^p convergence is needed

trigger: Slutsky misapplied where neither limit is a constant
symptom: claims (X_n, Y_n) -> (X, Y) jointly when X_n -> X in distribution and Y_n -> Y in distribution
root_cause: Slutsky requires Y_n to converge in probability to a constant, not just in distribution
resolution: show one component converges to a constant in probability, or work with the joint distribution directly via portmanteau

trigger: tower property used on non-sigma-algebra
symptom: applied E[E[X | F] | G] = E[X | F intersect G] without verifying F is contained in G
root_cause: the tower property requires nesting of sigma-algebras: E[E[X | G] | F] = E[X | F] only when F is contained in G
resolution: verify the inclusion F is contained in G before invoking tower; otherwise compute the conditional expectation directly

trigger: confused conditional expectation with conditional probability
symptom: treated E[X | A] (event conditioning) as E[X | sigma(Y)] without measurable structure
root_cause: conditioning on an event with positive probability is a number; conditioning on a sigma-algebra is a random variable
resolution: decide whether you need a number or a random variable; for sigma-algebra conditioning verify measurability of the integrand

trigger: treated pairwise independence as mutual independence
symptom: wrote joint density as product of marginals after only checking pairs
root_cause: pairwise independence does not imply mutual independence; the joint density factorisation requires the latter
resolution: either prove all subsets factorise (mutual independence) or weaken the conclusion to a covariance-only argument

trigger: treated orthogonality of non-Gaussian variables as independence
symptom: Cov(X, Y) = 0 used to conclude independence
root_cause: uncorrelated does not imply independent except for jointly Gaussian distributions
resolution: prove independence via product distributions or characteristic functions; only invoke the Gaussian shortcut after verifying joint normality

trigger: split E[XY] = E[X] E[Y] without independence
symptom: factored expectation of product without justification
root_cause: the product expectation factorisation requires independence (or at least uncorrelatedness in the centred case)
resolution: verify independence; if only uncorrelated, work with covariance Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] - E[X] E[Y] and isolate the cross term

trigger: Bonferroni union bound applied with overcounting
symptom: summed P(A_i) for many overlapping events without acknowledging overlap
root_cause: the Bonferroni inequality is tight only when events are disjoint; overlap inflates the bound but does not invalidate it, however the proof step claimed equality
resolution: claim only an upper bound, not equality; if a tighter bound is needed, use inclusion-exclusion truncated at higher order

trigger: inclusion-exclusion off by one
symptom: switched signs in alternating sum or omitted boundary term
root_cause: inclusion-exclusion has alternating signs ending with the n-fold intersection; the proof skipped a term
resolution: rewrite the formula symbolically and check signs; verify base case n = 2 and induct cleanly

trigger: applied CLT to non-iid sums without Lindeberg
symptom: concluded asymptotic normality of sum X_i without checking Lindeberg's condition
root_cause: the Lindeberg-Feller CLT requires the negligibility condition on second moments outside any epsilon-window
resolution: verify Lindeberg's condition or apply Lyapunov's stronger condition with a (2 + delta)-th moment

trigger: missing Lindeberg condition for triangular array
symptom: applied CLT to a triangular array with a single dominating term
root_cause: Lindeberg ensures no individual term contributes too much to the variance
resolution: show max of individual variances divided by total variance vanishes; otherwise prove a Berry-Esseen-style rate

trigger: asymptotic rate stated without variance assumption
symptom: claims O(n^{-1/2}) rate without finite second moment
root_cause: the sqrt(n) CLT rate requires finite variance; heavy-tailed cases yield slower rates
resolution: verify finite variance; if absent, derive a stable-law limit or use a modified rate from generalised CLT

trigger: delta method applied at a critical point with zero derivative
symptom: asymptotic variance comes out zero
root_cause: first-order delta method fails when g'(theta) = 0; the leading term is second order
resolution: use the second-order delta method: sqrt(n) (g(theta_hat) - g(theta)) is O_p(n^{-1/2}) but variance behaves like n^{-1}; compute via Taylor of order two

trigger: MLE treated as unbiased in finite samples
symptom: claims E[theta_hat] = theta_0 for fixed n
root_cause: MLE is consistent and asymptotically unbiased but not necessarily unbiased in finite samples
resolution: weaken the statement to consistency or compute the finite-sample bias explicitly (e.g. for variance estimators)

trigger: Cramer-Rao bound stated for biased estimators
symptom: applied Var(W) >= 1/I(theta) to a biased estimator
root_cause: the standard Cramer-Rao bound requires the estimator to be unbiased; the biased version has a (d/dtheta E[W])^2 factor
resolution: use the biased version Var(W) >= (psi'(theta))^2 / I(theta) where psi(theta) = E[W]

trigger: ignored regularity conditions of the Fisher information identity
symptom: differentiated under the integral on a discrete or non-regular family
root_cause: Fisher information identities require differentiability of the density and validity of differentiating under the integral sign
resolution: verify regularity; for discrete families use the discrete analogue; for irregular families like uniform on (0, theta) use specialised techniques

trigger: Wald, score, LR equivalence claimed away from the null
symptom: treated the three statistics as exchangeable under arbitrary alternatives
root_cause: asymptotic equivalence holds under contiguous alternatives near the null; under fixed alternatives the statistics differ
resolution: restrict equivalence claim to local alternatives or use power computations specific to each statistic

trigger: p-value uniform under alternative
symptom: used uniform-on-[0,1] property of the p-value under H_1
root_cause: uniformity holds under the null; under the alternative the p-value distribution is stochastically smaller
resolution: limit the uniformity claim to H_0; for power analysis compute the alternative distribution explicitly

trigger: type I error rate inflated by multiple comparisons
symptom: tested many hypotheses at level alpha each without correction
root_cause: naive testing inflates family-wise error to roughly 1 - (1 - alpha)^m for m tests
resolution: apply Bonferroni or Holm-Bonferroni correction, or control FDR via Benjamini-Hochberg if appropriate

trigger: OLS standard errors used under heteroskedasticity
symptom: reported sigma^2 (X'X)^{-1} standard errors when residual variance varies
root_cause: the homoskedastic formula is inconsistent under heteroskedasticity
resolution: use heteroskedasticity-robust White / sandwich standard errors (HC0-HC3) or weighted least squares

trigger: OLS unbiasedness claimed despite endogeneity
symptom: concluded E[beta_hat] = beta even though regressors correlate with the error
root_cause: OLS unbiasedness requires E[epsilon | X] = 0; endogeneity breaks this
resolution: use instrumental variables, control functions, or two-stage least squares to address the endogeneity

trigger: Gauss-Markov optimality claimed under heteroskedasticity
symptom: claimed OLS is BLUE without homoskedastic assumption
root_cause: the Gauss-Markov theorem requires Var(epsilon) = sigma^2 I
resolution: use generalised least squares (GLS) or White-corrected inference; OLS remains unbiased but is no longer minimum variance

trigger: F-statistic distributional claim violated by non-normal errors
symptom: stated F-statistic is exactly F-distributed for any error distribution
root_cause: exact F distribution requires normal errors; for non-normal errors only asymptotic F (or chi-squared) holds
resolution: either assume normal errors or rely on asymptotic chi-squared / bootstrap; report robustness assumptions explicitly

trigger: leverage trace identity used with rank-deficient X
symptom: claimed tr(H) = p when X has rank less than p
root_cause: tr(H) = rank(X), not p, when X is rank deficient
resolution: use rank(X) in place of p; address rank deficiency by dropping collinear columns or regularising

trigger: Gaussian conjugacy used with unknown variance
symptom: used the closed-form normal posterior for mu while sigma^2 was also unknown
root_cause: normal-normal conjugacy with closed form requires known variance; jointly modelling mu and sigma^2 yields a normal-inverse-gamma posterior
resolution: use the normal-inverse-gamma conjugacy or a Jeffreys prior; integrate out variance to obtain a t-distributed marginal posterior for mu

trigger: improper prior treated as a probability distribution
symptom: took expectations under an improper prior as if it were normalised
root_cause: improper priors do not have a well-defined expectation; only the posterior may be proper
resolution: verify posterior propriety; report inferences only after the posterior is proper; for prior predictive use a proper prior or restrict the parameter space

trigger: BVM applied with non-regular model
symptom: claimed posterior asymptotic normality on a non-regular family (e.g. uniform on (0, theta))
root_cause: Bernstein-von Mises requires regularity (parametric model with smooth log-likelihood and identifiability)
resolution: treat boundary or non-regular cases with specialised theory (Pitman drift, exponential rate for boundary parameters)

trigger: KL divergence treated as symmetric distance
symptom: used KL(P, Q) = KL(Q, P) or used KL as if it satisfied the triangle inequality
root_cause: KL is asymmetric and does not satisfy the triangle inequality
resolution: use Jensen-Shannon or total variation if symmetry or metric properties are needed

trigger: Pinsker applied with unbounded log ratio
symptom: obtained a tighter bound than allowed because the log-likelihood ratio is unbounded
root_cause: Pinsker is sharp only for bounded log ratios; for unbounded ratios use exponential or Hellinger comparisons
resolution: use Hellinger distance bounds (TV <= sqrt(2) Hellinger) or refined Pinsker-type inequalities

trigger: data processing inequality used on non-Markov chain
symptom: claimed I(X; Z) <= I(X; Y) when Y is not a sufficient statistic for X about Z
root_cause: DPI requires the Markov chain X -> Y -> Z, i.e. Z conditionally independent of X given Y
resolution: verify the Markov property; if absent, Z may carry information about X not contained in Y

trigger: Hoeffding's inequality used with unbounded variables
symptom: applied to sum of variables without finite range
root_cause: Hoeffding requires X_i in [a_i, b_i] a.s.; unbounded variables need Bernstein or sub-Gaussian / sub-exponential variants
resolution: switch to Bernstein's inequality (variance + range) or sub-Gaussian / sub-exponential concentration based on MGF tail behaviour

trigger: Bernstein applied without variance proxy
symptom: used Bernstein bound but no variance term sigma_i^2 was estimated
root_cause: Bernstein requires both range M and variance sigma_i^2; missing variance gives only Hoeffding-type bound
resolution: estimate variance bound; if only the range is known, fall back to Hoeffding's inequality

trigger: Azuma applied without bounded increments
symptom: treated unbounded martingale increments as if Azuma-Hoeffding applied
root_cause: Azuma-Hoeffding requires |M_k - M_{k-1}| <= c_k a.s.
resolution: use Freedman's inequality (variance-based) or self-normalising martingale concentration

trigger: MGF used without verifying its existence
symptom: Chernoff bound P(X >= t) <= e^{-lambda t} M_X(lambda) invoked without checking M_X(lambda) < infinity
root_cause: the MGF may be infinite for heavy-tailed variables; Chernoff fails
resolution: use truncation plus Chebyshev, or characteristic function bounds, or quantile-based concentration

trigger: Borel-Cantelli first part assumed without summability
symptom: claimed P(infinitely often A_n) = 0 from sum P(A_n) < infinity but did not verify summability
root_cause: Borel-Cantelli I requires sum_n P(A_n) < infinity
resolution: verify the sum is finite; if not, the conclusion P(i.o.) = 0 does not follow

trigger: Borel-Cantelli second part without independence
symptom: claimed P(i.o. A_n) = 1 from divergent sum without independence assumption
root_cause: Borel-Cantelli II requires (mutual) independence of the events
resolution: verify independence or use the conditional Borel-Cantelli (Levy) variant

trigger: Glivenko-Cantelli used on non-iid data
symptom: claimed uniform a.s. convergence of empirical CDF for dependent data
root_cause: Glivenko-Cantelli is stated for iid samples; for dependent data use ergodic-theoretic or weakly-dependent versions
resolution: use stationary ergodic Glivenko-Cantelli or beta-mixing analogues with convergence rates

trigger: Donsker invariance principle without finite second moment
symptom: claimed Brownian bridge limit for empirical process with heavy-tailed data
root_cause: Donsker requires finite variance; heavier tails give stable-process limits
resolution: switch to alpha-stable invariance principles or use trimmed empirical processes

trigger: Skorokhod representation invoked on non-Polish space
symptom: constructed a.s. convergent representation on an unmeasurable / non-separable space
root_cause: Skorokhod's representation theorem requires a Polish (separable, complete) sample space
resolution: embed into a Polish space or use the Dudley-Wichura version with separately measurable random variables

trigger: Slutsky combined with vector limits in mismatched dimensions
symptom: summed X_n converges in distribution to X (in R^d) with Y_n converges in probability to constant c (in R^k) with d != k
root_cause: addition requires matching dimensions; Slutsky composition requires dimension compatibility
resolution: align dimensions; if d != k consider concatenation or block-wise application of Slutsky

trigger: Lehmann-Scheffe applied without completeness
symptom: claimed UMVUE uniqueness from Rao-Blackwell alone
root_cause: uniqueness requires a complete sufficient statistic; without completeness multiple unbiased phi(T) can coexist
resolution: verify completeness of T (often via exponential family lemmas)

trigger: Basu's theorem used without complete sufficiency
symptom: concluded ancillary independence from sufficiency alone
root_cause: Basu requires the sufficient statistic to be complete
resolution: verify completeness; without it, ancillaries may correlate with the sufficient statistic

trigger: Karlin-Rubin used on a family without monotone likelihood ratio
symptom: claimed UMP property from a non-MLR family
root_cause: Karlin-Rubin requires monotone likelihood ratio in T(X)
resolution: verify MLR; if it fails, no one-sided UMP test exists in general; consider unbiased tests instead

trigger: treated mode as mean for skewed posterior
symptom: summarised a heavily right-skewed posterior by its mode and reported it as the mean
root_cause: mode and mean diverge for skewed distributions
resolution: report mode and mean separately; for inference use posterior mean / median based on the loss function

trigger: identifiability assumed under infinite parameter space
symptom: claimed unique theta from a population objective without proving identifiability
root_cause: non-identifiable models have multiple optima; consistency arguments fail
resolution: prove identifiability via injectivity of the parameterisation, or restrict the parameter space until identifiable

trigger: Bayes factor compared improper priors
symptom: computed Bayes factor between two models with improper priors
root_cause: Bayes factors with improper priors involve undefined normalising constants
resolution: use proper priors, intrinsic Bayes factors, or fractional Bayes factors with calibration

trigger: score test computed at unrestricted MLE
symptom: evaluated score statistic at the unrestricted estimate
root_cause: the score test statistic is evaluated at the restricted MLE under the null hypothesis
resolution: evaluate the score and Fisher information under the null restriction

trigger: Wald test invariance under reparameterisation assumed
symptom: claimed identical Wald statistic across nonlinear reparameterisations
root_cause: the Wald test is not invariant to nonlinear parameterisation; the score and LR tests are
resolution: use the LR or score statistic when invariance under reparameterisation matters

trigger: ignored boundary case in induction
symptom: proof by induction omitted base case or boundary k = 0 / k = 1
root_cause: induction without a verified base case is incomplete
resolution: explicitly verify the smallest non-trivial case before invoking the inductive step

trigger: combinatorial overcount in Bonferroni after dependence
symptom: summed individual probabilities for highly dependent events as if disjoint
root_cause: Bonferroni is correct as an upper bound regardless of dependence, but proof claimed near-tightness despite strong overlap
resolution: use a refined inequality (e.g. Schwarz-Slepian or Kounias) when events are positively dependent

trigger: applied tower property across non-nested filtrations
symptom: wrote E[E[X | F] | G] = E[X | F intersect G] without verifying nesting
root_cause: the tower identity holds when one filtration contains the other; non-nested filtrations require the smaller intersection sigma-algebra
resolution: verify nesting; if absent, compute via the smallest sigma-algebra containing both (or do not collapse the iterated conditional)

trigger: score function mean nonzero under contamination
symptom: used E[score] = 0 even though the data-generating distribution is not in the model
root_cause: the score has mean zero only under the assumed parametric model; under model misspecification it is biased
resolution: use the sandwich (robust) variance and treat the limit as a pseudo-true value rather than the true theta

trigger: central moments computed without finite raw moments
symptom: expressed central moment as raw moment combination without confirming integrability
root_cause: central moments require the corresponding raw moments to be finite
resolution: verify integrability; for heavy-tailed cases work with truncated or fractional moments

trigger: asymptotic normality concluded under non-iid array without rate adjustment
symptom: rate sqrt(n) used for non-iid CLT
root_cause: rates depend on the variance growth; the right standardisation may differ from sqrt(n)
resolution: use s_n = sqrt(sum Var(X_i)) as the divisor and verify Lindeberg with respect to s_n^2

trigger: test statistic continuity assumption ignored
symptom: computed p-value via the survival function as if continuous when the statistic is discrete
root_cause: for discrete statistics the p-value is not exactly uniform under the null; randomised tests or mid-p values are needed
resolution: use exact discrete p-values, randomised tests, or report mid-p values; clearly state conservatism

trigger: iid assumption applied to autocorrelated data
symptom: claimed sample variance / Wald statistic without correcting for serial correlation
root_cause: iid CLT and variance formulas underestimate variability under positive autocorrelation
resolution: use HAC (Newey-West) standard errors or block bootstrap to account for dependence

trigger: asymptotic independence concluded from joint Gaussianity check on margins
symptom: checked marginals are Gaussian and concluded independence
root_cause: marginal Gaussianity does not imply joint Gaussianity; without joint Gaussianity uncorrelated does not imply independent
resolution: verify joint Gaussianity (e.g. via the joint characteristic function) before invoking the Gaussian-uncorrelated equivalence

trigger: differentiability of likelihood not verified at boundary
symptom: Fisher information computed at the boundary of the parameter space
root_cause: score and information are well-defined in the interior; boundary parameters require one-sided derivatives or specialised theory
resolution: restrict to interior or use Chernoff-style asymptotics for boundary parameters

trigger: uniform integrability assumed without proof
symptom: transferred convergence in probability to L^1 without UI verification
root_cause: Vitali / dominated convergence requires UI or a dominating function
resolution: verify UI via de la Vallee-Poussin (sup E[phi(|X_n|)] < infinity for some superlinear phi) or show |X_n| <= Y for integrable Y

trigger: Markov chain mixing time assumed implies independence
symptom: stationary distribution sampling treated as iid after one step
root_cause: MCMC samples are dependent; effective sample size is smaller than nominal
resolution: use ESS or autocorrelation-adjusted variance estimates; thin or run multiple chains for diagnostic

trigger: test of two-sided hypothesis using one-sided p-value
symptom: reported one-sided p but conclusion was two-sided
root_cause: one-sided and two-sided p-values differ by a factor of two for symmetric statistics
resolution: double the one-sided p (for symmetric continuous tests) or recompute the two-sided p directly

trigger: pooled variance used despite unequal variances
symptom: applied two-sample pooled t-test under heteroscedasticity
root_cause: the pooled estimator is appropriate under equal variance; otherwise Welch's test is preferable
resolution: use Welch's t-test with the Satterthwaite degrees of freedom approximation

trigger: normal approximation to binomial used at small sample size
symptom: approximated Binomial(n, p) by N(np, np(1-p)) for very small np or n(1-p)
root_cause: the rule of thumb requires np and n(1-p) both at least 5 or 10
resolution: use the exact binomial p-value or the Wilson / Clopper-Pearson interval for small samples

trigger: Bayesian credible interval reported as confidence interval
symptom: interpreted a credible interval as having frequentist coverage
root_cause: credible and confidence intervals coincide only in special cases (e.g. flat prior on a Gaussian mean)
resolution: report as credible interval and, if needed, separately compute a frequentist confidence interval

trigger: MLE found at saddle point of log-likelihood
symptom: first-order condition satisfied but Hessian indefinite
root_cause: first-order conditions detect critical points; the maximum requires the Hessian to be negative semi-definite
resolution: verify the Hessian (or use boundary checks); restart optimisation from different points to escape saddles

trigger: Lindeberg condition verified only for fixed truncation
symptom: checked second moments outside one specific epsilon-window only
root_cause: Lindeberg requires the limit as epsilon -> 0 of negligibility, not at one fixed epsilon
resolution: show negligibility for every epsilon > 0; apply Lyapunov as a stronger sufficient condition

trigger: central moments mismatched with empirical moments
symptom: subtracted the population mean from the empirical mean before computing moments
root_cause: centring should use the same source consistently: either both population or both empirical
resolution: decide whether the moment is population or empirical; centre with the corresponding mean

trigger: asymptotic chi-squared assumed for boundary-of-parameter-space tests
symptom: claimed standard chi-squared limit when the null places the parameter on the boundary
root_cause: boundary nulls produce mixtures of chi-squared distributions (Chernoff's theorem)
resolution: use the appropriate chi-squared mixture or simulate the null distribution

trigger: regression intercept dropped without centring
symptom: ran OLS without intercept while predictors are not centred
root_cause: removing the intercept forces the regression line through the origin and biases coefficients toward absorbing the mean
resolution: include an intercept or centre the predictors and response before fitting

trigger: hypothesis tested twice on the same data without correction
symptom: performed exploratory test, then confirmatory test, on the same sample
root_cause: data dredging inflates type I error; selective inference rules apply
resolution: split data into exploratory and confirmatory subsets, or apply a selective inference correction

trigger: applied bootstrap percentile interval to a non-pivotal statistic
symptom: treated bootstrap percentile interval as having proper coverage
root_cause: the percentile method requires approximate pivotality; otherwise t-percentile or BCa intervals are needed
resolution: use studentised or BCa bootstrap intervals; verify pivotality before percentile

trigger: multivariate normal CDF treated as product of marginals
symptom: computed P(all X_i <= x_i) as product of P(X_i <= x_i)
root_cause: the joint CDF factorises over independent components only
resolution: use multivariate normal CDF (e.g. Genz algorithm) when components are correlated

trigger: robust standard errors used without large-sample size
symptom: applied HC0 / sandwich variance with very small n
root_cause: robust standard errors are asymptotic; finite-sample corrections HC2/HC3 perform better with small n
resolution: use HC2/HC3 finite-sample corrections; consider Bell-McCaffrey or wild bootstrap with cluster

trigger: concentration inequality applied to non-independent data without dependence-aware bounds
symptom: Hoeffding/Bernstein bound used directly on dependent X_i
root_cause: concentration inequalities for sums require independence or bounded dependence (e.g. mixing, martingale structure)
resolution: use martingale concentration (Azuma, McDiarmid) or mixing-based concentration with rate-dependent bounds
